title: Suno AI Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
summary: A Suno review helps you evaluate if the current audio fidelity and licensing terms meet your specific professional requirements for music production.
body_markdown:
## Suno pricing and commercial usage rights


Suno’s current subscription model separates users by generation volume and legal ownership. High-output creators pay for the indemnity required for professional distribution.


### Basic vs Pro vs Premier plan breakdown


For the **12,000,000 monthly active users**[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2026/02/26/ai-music-platform-suno-reaches-2-million-subscribers-as-industry-backlash-grows/) currently engaging with the tool, the three-tier structure functions as a funnel, which means the platform is systematically converting casual visitors into paying customers.


50 credits daily are included in the Basic Plan. You're limited to roughly 10 song generations every 24 hours without the ability to roll over unused capacity, so users must log in daily to avoid wasting their allocated quota.


$10 a month for the Pro Plan includes 2,500 credits, giving the subscriber a fixed budget to experiment with AI-generated tracks, ensuring that costs remain predictable for hobbyists, so users can plan their creative output without fear of surprise overage charges.


You can generate approximately 500 songs and have the right to monetize the output on streaming platforms.


**10,000 credits monthly** are provided in the Premier Plan for $30, effectively quadrupling the creative output capacity compared to the entry-level tier, allowing power users to scale their production significantly, as they gain a much larger sandbox for iterative development.


You can produce roughly 2,000 tracks to find the specific generation that fits a professional brief.


### Understanding commercial ownership of AI tracks


Commercial ownership is restricted exclusively to paid subscribers, creating a legal firewall between hobbyist play and professional exploitation.


If you generate a track on the Basic plan, Suno retains the copyright. You can't upload that specific audio file to Spotify or use it in a monetized YouTube video without violating the Terms of Service.


> Commercial ownership is restricted exclusively to paid subscribers, creating a legal firewall between hobbyist play and professional exploitation.


**Only tracks generated while a Pro or Premier subscription is active are owned by the user.**


You must ensure your billing cycle is current before hitting "Create" on a final project. This distinction has converted **2,000,000 people** ([Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/conormurray/2026/02/26/ai-music-platform-suno-reaches-2-million-subscribers-as-industry-backlash-grows/) ) into paid subscribers, as the platform is now a commercial library.


### The cost per song at scale


Roughly $0.015 is the cost of a single musical idea under the Premier plan, making the barrier to entry for high-volume experimentation remarkably low, meaning that the financial risk of exploring an unsuccessful creative direction is negligible.


This makes it a negligible expense for rapid prototyping.


This low barrier to entry has resulted in a massive disparity between AI generation and human-curated libraries. According to Edm, Suno users generate **7 million tracks daily** .


The user base creates a library the size of the entire 100-million-song Spotify catalog every 14 days, indicating that the platform is generating an unprecedented volume of new music at a breakneck pace, which means the sheer scale of content is rapidly outpacing human curation.


The value of the tool is in the speed at which you can discard 99% of the output to find the one viable melody for further engineering, which means the user’s primary role shifts from composer to curator. The workflow prioritizes high-volume experimentation over perfectionism.
